purpose: Concept exploration only; not integrated into runtime
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE cohesive concept sheet of six transparent terrain-overlay compositions for the existing Mushroom Forest side-view game.
Input images: the two attached screenshots are STYLE REFERENCES only: match their hand-painted, dark outlined illustrated purple mushrooms, twisted ink-blue roots, tiny cyan fungi, moss and hanging teal ivy exactly. Do not reproduce the platforms or screenshot backgrounds.
Primary request: design organic vignette overlays that can be laid directly over existing walls, ceilings and corners to make the terrain feel alive. Each composition combines roots + moss + fungi + trailing foliage as one naturally connected small ecosystem. These are significantly richer compositions than isolated tiny mushroom icons, but restrained enough for gameplay.

Canvas: landscape, 3 columns x 2 rows, six separated compositions with generous transparent gutters. No labels, no text, no border. Genuine transparent background. Clean side-view game art, no perspective ground plane, no backdrop or cast shadow.

Left to right top row:
1. OUTER LEDGE CORNER: an asymmetric moss cap with one medium violet mushroom and two small cyan fungi, wrapping around an invisible upper-right terrain corner into a dark twisted root and a short tapered teal ivy curtain. Underlying stone omitted, letting existing terrain show through.
2. VERTICAL WALL GARDEN: slender upright dark root braid with two modest violet shelf mushrooms growing to the right, small cyan sprouts nestled in moss, and trailing tiny teal leaves. Clearly attached vertically, no flat shelf or platform base.
3. CEILING DRAPE: a shallow horizontal intertwined root crossing, patches of moss above, a few narrow hanging vines with tiny cyan tips and a little cluster of hanging purple fungi underneath. Irregular asymmetrical strands with plenty of air between, not a solid curtain.

Left to right bottom row:
4. INNER FLOOR-WALL CORNER: compact L-shaped root flare tucked at a wall foot; a violet mushroom on the floor at the elbow, cyan sprouts near it and wispy moss climbing the vertical arm. Keep the adjacent walking space open. Actual terrain omitted.
5. OUTER CEILING CORNER: roots curl around the lower right corner of an invisible overhead mass; a small violet shelf fungus on the vertical side and descending teal leaf strands from the underside; small dark ferns tucked into the joint.
6. WALL CREVICE BLOOM: an elongated asymmetric narrow cluster of purple mushrooms emerging from an ink-dark root knot, with scattered cyan pin mushrooms and several tiny teal leaf strings. Broad dark root contact area fades toward transparency for terrain blending.

Style/medium: closely match the supplied existing platform artwork: hand-painted 2D storybook dark fantasy, crisp organic silhouettes, deep indigo-black ink outlines, stylized winding roots, cool teal moss and jewel-violet caps. Fungi stems and caps are distinct at small scale. No photorealism, no 3D render, no material scan.
Lighting: restrained cyan bioluminescent accents and violet cap edges, never brilliant white. Most root mass nearly black indigo. Soft alpha along terrain-contact edges; retain crisp leaf and mushroom silhouettes.
Constraints: no separate boulders, stone tiles, floating islands, flat walkable ledges, giant mushrooms, landmarks, runes, doors, skulls or characters. Roots and moss sit mostly against terrain; only a few thin leaves and fungi project into air. Every design should be individual and organically irregular, with visibly transparent holes between roots and leaves. Keep each composition self-contained within its cell.
